bayanihan: Wrote this one about the Filipino tradition of bayanihan — whole villages used to carry each other's houses. Literally.
memento-mori: The Stoics kept a skull on the desk for a reason. Remember you die — it's the only way to remember to live.
death: Nobody gets to skip this one, so I made a track that looks it straight in the eye.
gnostic-gospels: There were gospels that didn't make the cut. This is about the ones history buried.
kapwa-the-soul-of-unity: Kapwa is a Filipino word we don't have in English — the idea that my self and your self were never separate to begin with.
banality-of-evil: Hannah Arendt watched a war criminal on trial and saw something scarier than a monster: an ordinary man following orders.
courage-to-be-disliked: Adler thought most of our misery comes from needing everyone's approval. This track is about putting that burden down.
dolce-far-niente: The Italians have a phrase for the sweetness of doing absolutely nothing. Turns out it's a skill.
che-guevara: Idealist, killer, icon, cautionary tale — Che was all four at once. That contradiction is the song.
the-anxious-generation: We ran an experiment on an entire generation of kids: childhood through a screen. The results are in.
voltaires-vision: Voltaire spent his life fighting certainty with doubt and dogma with wit. Still feels current.
making-sense: For everyone who's tried every framework and still lies awake — this one's about the search itself.
row-row-your-boat: You've sung this rhyme a hundred times without noticing it ends with 'life is but a dream.' Someone slipped philosophy into the nursery.
soul-ride: Consciousness isn't something you have, it's something you're riding. Made a track about the ride.
the-filter: Between you and reality sits a stack of filters — your senses, your feed, your habits. This is about what doesn't get through.
reaching-for-the-stars: On wanting more than the map says is reachable.
zoom-in-zoom-out: Every problem looks enormous until you zoom out. Every blessing looks small until you zoom in.
fugazi: Fake watches, fake feeds, fake fronts — a track about learning to smell what's fugazi.
the-cave: Plato said we're prisoners watching shadows and calling them the world. Turning around hurts. That's the track.
pleasure-vs-purpose: The oldest trade in the human ledger: feel good now, or mean something later.
the-art-of-asking: Asking for help feels like losing. It isn't — and this one's about why.
the-bureaucracy-trap: You are not a case number. A track about systems that process people instead of seeing them.
infinite-possbilities: Every second you're standing at a fork with infinite roads. Most of them close quietly while we scroll.
between-the-body-and-the-fabric: Where exactly do you end and the world begin? The border is blurrier than it looks.
shift-the-lens: Same life, different lens, completely different picture. On the art of reframing.
prison-of-the-will: What if the thing you call free will is also the thing holding the keys?
the-self-that-wasnt: Buddhists went looking for the self and found nobody home. Unsettling — then liberating.
the-illusion-of-no-escape: Half the locked doors in a life are painted on. This one's about testing the handle.
they-say-were-free: Free to choose — from a menu somebody else wrote. How free is that, really?
don-quixote-the-windmills-of-the-mind: Quixote charged windmills and everyone called him mad. Four centuries later we're still arguing about who saw clearly.
winners-keep-winning: Advantage compounds. A track about what that does to everyone standing at the bottom of the curve.
rise-and-fall: Empires, egos, markets, moods — everything that rises rehearses its fall.
